key_insight: Matching global force–displacement curves alone can conceal incorrect cohesive laws; spatial strain measurements substantially improve their identification.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports identification of spatially varying interface damage laws relevant to delamination and fiber–matrix debonding.
method: Represent cohesive laws with thermodynamically structured, physics-constrained neural networks in an intrinsic cohesive-zone finite element model.
Compute sensitivities using automatic differentiation and a discrete adjoint that accounts for damage history.
Regularize heterogeneous identification with a shared, low-dimensional learned prior and spatially varying latent coordinates.
evidence_signal: Numerical studies of double-cantilever beams and fiber–matrix composites evaluate constitutive recovery, including comparisons with bilinear cohesive models and Bayesian optimization.
watch_item: The evidence is numerical; reliable identification still depends on informative spatial strain measurements, even with a learned prior.
paper_title: A Differentiable Framework for Inverse Identification of Heterogeneous Cohesive Laws
